solution:
The correct answer is __**1) ic, ii-a, iii-b, iv-d**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Starch detection:** Iodine test is used to detect the presence of starch in food items. The iodine solution turns blue-black in the presence of starch.
 
• **Fat detection:** Acrolein test is used for the detection of fats in food items. This test involves heating the fat and detecting the acrolein formed, which has a pungent odor.
 
• **Protein detection:** Biuret test is used to identify the presence of protein. The reagent changes color from blue to violet in the presence of peptide bonds.
 
• **Halogenoalkane salts detection:** Silver nitrate test is used to detect halide ions in halogenoalkane salts. It forms a precipitate of silver halide.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Iodine Test for Starch:**

 
 
• When iodine solution is added to a sample containing starch, it forms a blue-black complex.
 
• This test is specific to polysaccharides like starch.
 
• The blue-black color is due to the formation of a starch-iodine complex.
 
 
 
• **Acrolein Test for Fats:**
 
 
• When fats are heated, glycerol is dehydrated to form acrolein, which has a distinctive odor.
 
• This test is often used in laboratory settings to confirm the presence of triglycerides.
 
 
 
• **Biuret Test for Proteins:**
 
 
• The Biuret reagent contains copper sulfate, which reacts with peptide bonds under alkaline conditions.
 
• A violet color indicates the presence of proteins due to the complex formation between copper ions and peptide bonds.
 
 
 
• **Silver Nitrate Test for Halides:**
 
 
• Silver nitrate solution reacts with halide ions to form a precipitate of silver halide.
 
• The color of the precipitate can help identify the specific halide (e.g., white for chloride, cream for bromide, yellow for iodide).
